newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian singer Fela critically ill, family.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian singer Fela critically ill, family.

text.p: Nigeria's maverick Afro-beat superstar Fela Anikulapo-Kuti has been critically ill for the past two weeks but refuses to see a doctor, family members said on Friday.

"It is the first time he has been as sick as this," his son Femi Anikulapo-Kuti told Reuters. "He is very weak, although there has been some improvement. He drinks a lot of fruit juice and can eat pepper soup."

A star of the international music scene in the 1970s and 80s, the 58-year-old Anikulapo-Kuti, known to fans as "Fela" won a reputation for smoking marijuana, sleeping with large numbers of women and dressing only in his underpants.

"With Fela you can never tell, he may spring back stronger than before. When we are at the house with the family he sometimes jumps up and says 'what are you all worried about get out and leave me to sleep'," said Femi, also a musician.

Since falling ill, Fela has been confined to his house in the working class Ikeja district of Lagos, where he is cared for by an elder sister and a daughter. Numerous other women drift around the house where the smell of marijuana lingers.
Both Western and traditional Nigerian medicine have been rejected by Fela, who refuses to see a doctor.

Nigerian newspapers have suggested that Fela is close to death and that, given a lifestyle which led him to marry more than two dozen women, he could be suffering from AIDS -- increasingly common in the populous African nation.

"I don't think it is AIDS and in any case it is nothing to be ashamed of and he is not a criminal, not a bad man. If he had AIDS my father would be the first to say so," said Femi. "But he has never had any medical tests so we could not know."
On several occasions Fela was locked up by dissaproving Nigerian military regimes who didn't take kindly to being portrayed as of low intelligence in his lyrics.

But for the past two years he has only performed rarely at his club, known as "The Shrine", and he has not challenged military ruler General Sani Abacha. His younger brother Beko Ransome-Kuti is in jail for alleged involvement in a coup.
Fela was detained earlier this year by the anti-narcotics agency, before being released after the agency said efforts to counsel him for his long-term drug habit had failed.
